content.title: Masters 2026 cut line tracker: The 18th took a toll on the stars
content.text: Updated April 10, 2026, 7:42 p.m. ETIt was a wild second round at the 2026 Masters, and the action on the leaderboard – and the projected cut line – was non-stop.The field of 91 golfers was reduced to the low 50 and ties, which wound up being 54 golfers who finished at 4 over par or better. Those golfers will be around for the weekend, while everyone else is packing up early, heading home.2026 Masters Tournament leaderboardStay up to date with tee times and pairings, as well as scores, throughout the weekend.Notable players who missed the cut at the 2026 MastersIt's a lenghty list of notable golfers who fells short of the low 50 and ties at Augusta National in 2026.The weekend field at the 2026 Masters is set (7:12 p.m.)While Rory McIlroy made it look easy, making birdie on six of the last seven holes at Augusta National on Friday evening, other players who were just trying to make the cut struggled. Bryson DeChambeau made a seven on the 18th to miss the cut by two shots. Akshay Bhatia made a double-bogey six to miss the cut by two as well. Alex Noren made a bogey on the 17th to lift his score to +4, forcing the Swede, who was playing in the last group of the day, to make par in order to make the cut and qualify for the weekend at the 2026 Masters.Noren's tee shot went right, into the first cut, and then his approach shot sailed to the back-left portion of the green. He was able to two-putt, score a par and make the cut on the number at 4 over (148).In the end, 54 players finished at 4 over or better and qualified for the third and fourth rounds at the 2026 Masters.Bye-Bye Bryson (6:30 p.m.)Bryson DeChambeau held steady at 3 over after making birdie on 15 and seemed poised to make the cut at the 2026 Masters, but the 18th hole at Augusta National proved to be his downfall. His tee shot went right, into the pine straw, and then his second shot finished in the bunker that guards the front-left portion of the green. As he did on Thursday on the 11th hole, DeChambeau struggled with the sand and needed two shots to get out, with his second shot rolling off the front of the green. His fifth shot was a pitch back to the hole that went 12 feet past the cup on the right. He missed the putt and tapped in for seven and a final score of 6 over, two shots over the cut line.Bhatia blows it (6:20 p.m.)Akshay Bhatia holed out from a bunker on 17 to reach 3 over and seemed safe with the cut line at 4 over, but then made a double-bogey 6 on the 18th hole after his tee shot went right into the trees. Bhatia punched out to the fairway, but his third shot came up short and right of the green. His pitch shot rolled 11 feet past the hole, and he missed it left, on the high side, to finish at +6, two shots above the cut line.Crunch Time (5:45 p.m.)We have 54 players who are currently at 4 over or better, but afer Bubba Watson missed a birdie putt on the 18th hole that would have dropped his score to -4, the two-time Masters winner finished at 5 over and will miss the cut at the 2026 Masters.Bryson DeChambeau was sitting on the cut line at 4 over but made a birdie on the par-5 15th and has moved to 3 over, giving the two-time U.S. Open winner a bit of a cushio as he completes his second round.Akshay Bhatia is at 5 over playing the 17th hole after making bogey on 16, and Alex Noren is still at 5 over as he plays the 13th.The magic number should be -4 (5 p.m.)As of 5 p.m. Eastern, there were 56 players at the 2026 Masters with a score of 4 over or better, and according to Data Golf, there was a 99.2 percent chance that score would be the cut number.A birdie on the par-5 15th hole moved 2012 and 2014 Masters champion Bubba Watson to 4 over, while Bryson DeChambeau, Viktor Hovland and Patrick Cantlay are each at 3 over as they finish the back nine at Augusta National.Rasmus Højgaard came to the 18th hole at 5 over. The Dane stepped up to the tee, hit a great drive and then nailed his approach shot to 10 feet and made the birdie putt to reach 4 over. Playing in one of the last groups of the day, Sweden's Alex Noren was 6 over par through nine holes, then made a birdie on 10 to reach 5 over. With two par 5s to play, he could still make the cut if he's able to get another birdie and avoid bogeys.Danny Willett and J.J. Spaun finished earlier at 5 over, and it appears they will miss out on a chance to play the weekend by one shot.It's time to grind for major winners (4:30 p.m.)While Rory McIlroy, Patrick Reed and Xander Schauffele play the back nine at Augusta National and contend atop the leaderboard, several big-name players find themselves on the cut line, which remains at 4 over. The low 50 players and ties qualify to play the weekend at the Masters, and as of 4:30 p.m. Eastern, 54 golfers had scores of +4 or better, including 2011 Masters champion Charl Schwartzel, who is at 4 over through 17 holes.Cameron Smith, winner of the 2022 British Open, made a costly bogey at 14 that elevated his score to 5 over, while two-time Masters champion Bubba Watson made birdies on 12 and 13 to reach 5 over, one shot above the cut line with four holes to play.4 over is holding (4 p.m.)As of 4 p.m. Eastern, there were 55 golfers with a score of 4 over or better at the 2026 Masters, and DataGolf.com is giving +4 a 90 percent chance of finishing as the cut line number. If that holds, 2025 U.S. Open champion J.J. Spaun would miss the cut by a shot after posting 74-75 (149), as would 2016 Masters champion Danny Willett.Jon Rahm, winner of the 2022 Masters, bounced back from a 78 on Thursday to shoot 70 on Friday and finish at 4 over, so the two-time major winner appears likely to make the cut. Bryson DeChambeau is bouncing back after shooting 76 on Thursday and is now at 3 over.Early cut line projection: 4 over (3 p.m.)As of 3 p.m. ET, DataGolf.com has the projected cut line moving to 4 over par, after opening the day at 5 over. We're all but cemented in at that number as there is now only a 13 percent chance it might move to 3 under. Jordan Spieth will make the cutAfter missing the cut in two of his last five starts at Augusta National, Jordan Spieth is safely inside the cut line on Friday as he sits at even par after 15 holes. Spieth opened Friday with a birdie and then made 10 straight pars before posting a bogey on No. 12.On the par-4 ninth, Spieth pulled his tee shot and it appeared to be heading for the trees but a patron under the tree could be seen reacting after getting hit by the golf ball. Spieth signed a golf glove and went over to give it to the man, whose deflection helped Spieth save par on the hole.Of course, the Texan captured the green jacket in 2015, but he also has four other top-4 finishes at Augusta National. J.J. Spaun slipping early on FridayAfter winning the Valero Texas Open last weekend, it appeared that J.J. Spaun was ready for a big week at Augusta National. Instead, he's trending in the wrong direction and, as of 11:45 a.m. ET, Spaun is about even money to miss the cut.Spaun is 3 over through his first seven holes and sits at 5 over for the tournament. He has about 50 percent odds to make the third round. In 2022, after winning the Valero, Spaun finished T-22 and in his only other appearance last year, he finished 50th.UPDATE (3 p.m. ET): Spaun finished the day at 5 over and it likely to miss the cut. Robert MacIntyre still looking in from outsideIt's been a rough week for Robert MacIntyre, who was leading the Valero Texas Open last Sunday, but surrendered the title to J.J. Spaun. On Thursday, MacIntyre declined to speak with reporters after signing his scorecard. His 8-over 80 puts him five shots outside the projected cut line to begin Friday's second round. Microphones also caught MacIntyre swearing on the 12th and 13th holes, and he slammed his clubs on the 17th, his final bogey of the day. And he was seen flipping off one of Augusta's greens.As of 2:15 p.m. ET, McIntyre is 1 under on the day, but he's still 7 over for the tournament and has about a 10 percent chance of making the cut. Bryson DeChambeau hoping to make historyNo player has ever won the Masters after making a triple-bogey or worse, and Bryson DeChambeau did just that on Thursday, failing to get out of the bunker on the 11th hole in his first two attempts. He finished the day with a 76, his worst score at the course since his second round in 2022, when he missed the cut after an ugly 80.He'll need to make up some lost ground on Friday. He starts the day right at the projected cut line at 4 over."Just going to give what the golf course gives me. I have to try to hit my irons better," he said. "I drove it left numerous occasions. Did a great job on 18. Wind didn't hurt it like we thought, and that's this game. That's the golf course." Can Jon Rahm make the weekend?Jon Rahm opened with a par in his second round on Friday and then added a birdie on the second and, as of 2:20 p.m. ET, was still at 5 over for the tournament. He did, however, birdie the 16th hole to get to 4 over, which should be enough for him to make it right on the number.Rahm, who won the 2023 Masters, is no stranger to slow starts at Augusta National. Since winning his second major title three springs ago, Rahm has opened over par every time since, the latest effort resulting in a 6-over 78 on a Thursday that had Rahm searching for answers between every swing."It's a hard golf course. Some of the players might have been able to manage a respectable round, but when you have no feel with the swing whatsoever, it's just not an easy one," Rahm said. Fred Couples struggled on backEveryone is rooting for Fred Couples, who was 2-under after 14 holes on Thursday, to make the cut. Unfortunately, Couples carded a 9 on No. 15 in the opening round, and compounded the damage at the 16th with another water ball. In all, the 1992 Champ played Nos. 15-17 in 8-over. He posted an opening round 78 after a pair of closing double bogeys.He birdied the second hole on Friday, however, and as of 10:45 a.m. ET, he's right on the cut line at 5 over.UPDATE (1:45 p.m.): Couples limped home and sits at 8 over, meaning he will not be able to reach the weekend.Did his missing the cut change Couples' view of Augusta National? Absolutely not."You would have to be an idiot not to love Augusta National. I don't know if you can use those words, but they might like that, hearing that," Couples said. "You know, as a kid you grow up watching it. I can't tell you, you know, Ed Sneed and what he did, Hubert Green, and then Jack Nicklaus winning and Tom Weiskopf. Those were all the greats. Weiskopf, Green, Sneed, they never won, and maybe they should have."Then you come here, and you finally see it, and you go, you know, it's -- I mean, the only other guy I've really heard use the same words is Phil. It's like paradise. People love it, but I consider it to be just the greatest walk you could ever have. There are great courses all over the world, but there are none of them like this." Bubba Watson likely to miss cutFour bogeys on the front will likely prove insurmountable for Bubba Watson, who is making his 18th appearance at Augusta National. As of 3:30 p.m. ET, Watson is 2 over for the day and 6 over for the tournament, meaning he'll have to make a few more birdies on the last few holes to finish on the right side.Watson is one of 18 players to have won the Masters more than once, and although he did make a birdie on the 12th hole when he stuck his tee shot to eight feet and drained the putt, he still is on the outside looking in. Patrick Cantlay opened the day about even to make the cutPatrick Cantlay has never won the Masters, although he has finished in the top 25 on four different occasions. Heading into the second round of play, Cantlay has about 40 percent odds of reaching the weekend, according to betting sites. Cantlay, who starts his tee on the first tee at 1:56 p.m. ET is 6 over after the opening round of play. He has only missed the cut once since 2018. Tom McKibbin misses the cut in Augusta debutIt was a rough two days for Tom McKibbin, who was making his Masters debut. The LIV Golf player finished 7 over through 36 holes and will head home early. He was surprised by the difficulty of the course."I liked every hole. Every hole was pretty good," he said. "It's hard to beat that 11, 12, 13. Those are pretty iconic holes, but I think people on TV maybe don't realize how hard some of the shots are. I certainly didn't. I sort of had heard how hard they were, but when you watch it on TV, you cannot see any of the slopes on the fairways and even the greens. The greens don't look as slopey as they are and then once you stand over the ball with a long iron or a wood, I mean, it feels so strange. You never get it anywhere else." Rasmus Hojgaard had little chance of making the weekendRasmus Hojgaard opened the day at 6 over after a rough Thursday at Augusta National. His odds to make the cut as of 10 a.m. ET are about one in five, meaning he'll need to get rolling early to survive. Hojgaard's only other Masters appearance came last year, when he finished T-32 and he hasn't missed the cut in his last six majors.How did he get in such a predicament this time around? Shots like this didn't help.His brother, Nicolai, is also in danger of missing out as he posted bogeys on two of the first five holes and made the turn on Friday at 6 over for the tournament.UPDATE: Rasmus rallied and as of 2:30 p.m. ET, he's at 4 over for the tournament, and barely on the right side of the cut line. What player even or better has the worst odds to make the cut?So there are plenty of players trying to play their way up the leaderboard and into the weekend, but the task is equally as daunting for some who are clinging to the hope they'll stick around for the final two rounds of the Masters.We looked at the odds of players who opened the day at even or better to see which has the most potential to slip out of the weekend. And the answer was ...Max Homa. Despite shooting an even-par 72, the affable Californian had nearly even odds to slip out of the top 50 and ties by day's end. Homa teed off at 11:03 a.m. on Friday.UPDATE (1:45 p.m. ET): After nine holes of play on Friday, Homa is 1 under for the round and now has a 98 percent chance of making the cut.Where to watch the second round of the 2026 MastersFeatured groups and featured holes coverage start at 8:45 a.m. ET on Masters.com, the ESPN app, Paramount+ and Prime Video, which also then takes over as the main TV feed for two hours before kicking it over to ESPN.Prime Video: 1-3 p.m. ETESPN/ESPN App: 3-7:30 p.m. ETWatch the Masters on Prime Video Watch the Masters on ESPNHow does the cut work at the Masters?Starting in 2020, the Masters went to a cut rule of the low 50 and ties. Only those golfers qualify for the final 36 holes.The cut rules at changed a bit over the years at Augusta National.2013-2019: Low 50 scores and anyone within 10 shots of the leader.1962 - 2012: Low 44 and anyone with 10 shots1957-1961: Low 40 and ties1934-1956: There was no cut at the Masters The Masters cut: What has been the cut number in the past?The cutline changes from year to year, based on the weather and scoring conditions.2025: 3-over 1472024: 7-over 1512023: 4-over 1482022: 5-over 1492021: 4-over 1482020: 1-over 145Who's in danger of missing the cut after 18 holes?It's only been 18 holes but the top-50-and-ties cutoff would be 3 over and that would leave a lot of big names out of the weekend fun. Here are some big names who have work to do on Friday:Bubba Watson, 4 overBryson DeChambeau, 4 overSungjae Im, 4 overDaniel Berger, 4 overPatrick Cantlay, 5 overMin Woo Lee, 6 overJon Rahm, 6 overRobert MacIntyre, 8 overWhat's the weather forecast for Augusta on Friday?It should be a pretty great weather day at Day 2 of the Masters with an expected high of 77 and just about a 10 percent chance of rain, according to AccuWeather.
